newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees possible tender on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees possible tender on Busang.

text.p: Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister discussed the rich gold property Busang with President Suharto on Friday and said there was a possibility of seeking tenders to develop the site if Canadian companies Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp failed to agree.
"There is time, but if they fail we will find a way that most benefits the country," Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana told reporters.
"One option is a tender...it could be an international tender. Until now, I have not got a report from them. We must be patient, there is time," Sudjana said.

He said the government had sent a letter to both companies on January 15 telling them to settle with their Indonesian partners before getting the go-ahead to further explore and develop the huge Busang find in West Kalimantan province.
A source close to negotiations between Barrick and Bre-X said on Wednesday he expected the two companies to strike a deal by the end of this week.
Bre-X estimates Busang contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.
"We hoped they would report the result on February 15. But we knew that February 15 is a (Saturday) holiday, so we hope to get the report...on February 17," Sudjana said.
"In my letter I said that if they failed to agree, all things that had been discussed between related parties with the mines and energy department were not valid," Sudjana said.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to partner Barrick, and the Mines and Energy Ministry said in December they had agreed to split Busang, with 22.5 percent going to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick and the rest to the government.

Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought a 50-percent stake in two companies with minority interests in two of the Busang areas.
Barrick has an alliance with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardijanti Rukmana.
